h1: Starting a digital marketing career in India
metaTitle: How Can I Start Digital Marketing as a Career?
metaDescription: Starting a digital marketing career in India: the role to apply for, the portfolio that gets replies, where jobs are posted, and real year-one pay.
answer: Start by applying for one named role, not "digital marketing". Paid media associate and content executive are the two roles that genuinely hire freshers in India, because both produce supervisable output from week one. Build three proof artefacts, expect ₹2.4–₹4.2 lakh in year one, and take the job with the most reps.
takeaways: Generalist applications get filtered. Recruiters hire against one specific gap, and "open to any role" reads as "has no skill yet".
The portfolio that gets replies is a live project, a dashboard and a teardown of the employer's own marketing — not a Canva PDF.
Year one in a metro: roughly ₹2.4–₹4.2 lakh. Tier-2 lower. Funded startups occasionally higher for candidates with a live project.
Job one should be chosen for **reps**, not title or pay. An agency gives you more accounts in a year than a brand gives you in three.

sections.h2: Apply for one job, not the whole department
body: The most common fresher mistake in Indian marketing hiring is the application that says "seeking a role in digital marketing, open to SEO, social media, content, ads or analytics". It feels flexible. It reads as untrained.

Recruiters aren't hiring a marketer. They're filling a specific hole — nobody is writing the ad copy, or nobody is watching the Google Ads account, or the blog hasn't shipped in two months. When your application doesn't name that hole, someone else's does, and theirs gets the call.
So pick one. You can change specialism at year two, and most people do. What you can't do is get hired for all five at once when you've done none of them.

callout.title: The line that kills applications
callout.body: "I am a quick learner with a keen interest in digital marketing." Every fresher writes it, which means it carries zero information. Replace it with one sentence naming a number you moved on a real account, however small. ₹4,000 of ad spend at a ₹180 cost per lead beats any adjective.

sections.h2: The two roles that actually take freshers
body: Not all entry-level marketing roles are equally open. Two hire consistently in India, for the same structural reason: the output is visible within a week, so a manager can supervise a beginner without risking much.

table.caption: Where freshers actually get hired in Indian digital marketing.
head: Role
What you do in month one
What they screen for
rows: Paid media associate / PPC executive
Building campaigns, adding negatives, pulling reports, writing ad variants under supervision
Google Ads certification, a live campaign you've run yourself, comfort with numbers in a spreadsheet
Content executive / content writer
Briefs, drafts, on-page basics, publishing in the CMS, updating old posts
Published writing samples in the category, evidence you understand search intent, speed
SEO executive (third, slower)
Keyword research, on-page fixes, internal links, reporting
A site you've ranked something on. Hardest to prove as a fresher because results take months
Social media executive (crowded)
Calendars, community, basic editing, reels
A real account you grew. Heaviest applicant volume, so the bar on proof is highest

bullets: **Paid media is the fastest on-ramp** because your competence is provable with screenshots. Cost per lead is a number a stranger can verify in ten seconds.
**Content is the widest door** because demand is constant and the sample is the interview. Ten good published pieces beat a degree.
**Marketing analytics** takes almost no freshers directly, but it's where the money goes later. Learn GA4 early and you can move into it at year two.

body: Nobody reads a 14-slide Canva deck about your "skills". Three artefacts do the persuading, and each one takes a weekend.
numbered: **One live project write-up.** A real account — a family business, a clinic, an NGO, your own store. Starting number, what you changed, what happened, what failed. The failure is the most credible line in the document and it's the one everybody omits.
**A dashboard you built.** Looker Studio is free. It proves you can measure, which is the single most common gap in fresher applications and the easiest one to close.

**A teardown of the company you're applying to.** Their site speed, their ad copy, three specific fixes with reasoning and screenshots. Attach it to the application email. The reply rate on this is not close to the reply rate on a normal CV, and almost nobody does it because it takes effort per application.

sections.h2: Where the roles are actually posted
body: Application volume on the big boards is brutal, so route selection matters as much as the CV itself.
bullets: **Naukri and LinkedIn** — highest volume, lowest reply rate. Worth doing, not worth relying on. Apply within a few hours of the post going up; lists get long fast.
**Instahyre, Cutshort, Wellfound** — startup-weighted, better signal-to-noise, and recruiters actually read profiles here.
**Agency careers pages, directly.** Most Indian agencies hire continuously and post late or not at all. A cold email with a teardown attached beats a board application by a wide margin.
**Internshala** for internships, which remain a legitimate entry route if the stipend is real and the work isn't just posting reels.
**Marketing communities and Telegram/WhatsApp job groups** — smaller pools, faster decisions, and often the same three people posting every good role in a city.
**Referrals**, still the highest-converting channel. Which is an argument for being visible: writing publicly about what you're learning does more for your first job than another certificate.

sections.h2: Agency, brand or startup for job one
body: This choice compounds more than the salary does, because it decides how many times you get to practise in year one.

For most people the agency is the right first job and the wrong third one. You want volume of reps while your salary is low enough that mistakes are cheap. What an agency actually does day to day is covered in [how SEO agencies work](/answers/how-do-seo-agencies-work) — worth reading before an agency interview, because most candidates can't describe the business model of the company they're applying to.

body: Ranges, not promises — Indian marketing pay varies more by city and funding stage than by your skill in the first year.

In metros, most first offers land between **₹2.4 and ₹4.2 lakh a year**. Agencies sit at the lower end, in-house brands slightly higher, funded startups highest, occasionally to ₹6 lakh for someone arriving with a live project and a paid media certification. Tier-2 cities generally run 30–40% below metro bands, though remote roles have compressed that gap.

The number that matters more is year three. Marketing pay in India is barbelled — crowded and cheap at entry, genuinely short of people at senior specialist level. The same pattern shows up clearly in the [SEO salary picture in India](/answers/what-is-the-salary-of-seo-in-india), and it's the reason the first two years are best treated as paid training rather than income.

callout.title: How to check these ranges yourself
callout.body: Don't take anyone's salary table on faith, including this one. Open ten live listings for the exact role and city today, note the posted bands, and ask two people already doing the job. That's a better dataset than any published average, because it's current and it's yours.

sections.h2: The first six months on the job
body: Once you're in, the compounding starts with access. Everything you can learn is downstream of what you're allowed to touch.
numbered: **Ask for read access to everything in week one** — the ad accounts, Search Console, GA4, the CRM. Nobody refuses a fresher who wants to read. Most freshers never ask.
**Own one number publicly.** Volunteer to report it weekly. Owning a number is how you stop being the person who does tasks and start being the person who has a track record.
**Learn the money side early.** Cost per acquisition against margin, not cost per click. Marketers who understand the P&L get promoted past marketers who understand the platform.
**Write down what you did and what happened.** Six months in, that document is your next application, and you will not remember the details otherwise.
**Refuse nothing technical.** The tracking setup, the tag manager job, the messy migration — that's the work everyone avoids and it's where the specialism nobody can hire for starts.

faqs.q: Can I get a digital marketing job with no experience?
faqs.a: Yes, but not with no evidence. Run one real account — a family business, an NGO, your own store — and document the before-and-after. A fresher with a ₹5,000 campaign they can explain beats a fresher with four certificates and nothing to show, every time.

faqs.q: Which digital marketing role should a fresher apply for?
faqs.a: Paid media associate or content executive. Both produce visible output within a week, so managers can supervise a beginner cheaply. Social media roles get the most applicants for the fewest seats, and analytics rarely hires freshers directly.

faqs.q: Do I need a degree or an MBA to start in digital marketing?
faqs.a: No. It's one of the few Indian white-collar fields where portfolio genuinely outranks credential at entry level. An MBA helps later for brand-side and leadership roles, and does almost nothing for a first performance-marketing job.

faqs.q: What salary should a fresher expect in digital marketing in India?
faqs.a: Roughly ₹2.4–₹4.2 lakh a year in metros, with agencies at the lower end and funded startups higher. Tier-2 cities typically run 30–40% below that. Verify against ten current listings for your exact role and city rather than trusting any published average.

faqs.q: Is an agency or an in-house job better to start with?
faqs.a: An agency, usually. You'll touch five to fifteen accounts in year one instead of one, and you want that volume of practice while mistakes are still cheap. The trade is pace, servicing overhead and burnout risk, which is why it's a great first job and a poor third one.

faqs.q: How long before I'm actually good at this?
faqs.a: Twelve to eighteen months to work unsupervised, three years to be genuinely valuable. The gap between entry and senior is where Indian marketing pay stops being crowded, so treat the first two years as paid training and optimise for reps over rupees.
